plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.description: In the Australian summer, this shrub of the eastern bush puts on a festive show. Tiny cream flowers open in airy clusters. Their petals fade, and the sepals swell and turn a brilliant crimson. The whole plant looks as if it has been decorated for the holidays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Flowers appear in November and December. The red sepals stay colorful until about February.
plants.location: Coastal and mountain bushland of New South Wales, Australia, and in gardens across the region
plants.funFact: The 'flower' you see at Christmas is mostly the enlarged calyx, which turns red after the small white petals drop. Australians cut branches for holiday decorations, so the plant has become a southern-hemisphere Christmas tradition.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In the wild, poinsettia is a tall, leggy shrub or small tree that can reach 3–4 meters. At the tips of its branches it carries bursts of scarlet leaf-like bracts. These surround tiny yellow-green true flowers. The result is a blaze of color in the winter dry season.
plants.bloomingSeason: The wild shrubs bloom in December, in the northern-hemisphere winter.
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America, and grown worldwide as a holiday plant
plants.funFact: The bright red 'petals' are modified leaves called bracts. The true flowers are the small yellow clusters (cyathia) at their center. The Aztecs called the plant cuetlaxochitl and used it for dye and traditional medicine.
